warning: These questions are exploratory probes, not an accessibility or security conformance standard, nor a formal W3C questionnaire.

questions.prompt: Does the project describe accessible experiences and known accessibility barriers?
questions.why: Documentation and existing issues may disclose barriers, but do not establish a complete assessment.

questions.prompt: Can essential tasks be completed using different input modalities?
questions.why: Keyboard, pointer, speech and touch interactions may need testing beyond source inspection.

questions.prompt: Are accessibility semantics, labels and alternative content provided where relevant?
questions.why: Look for accessible names, semantic structures, captions and alternatives.

questions.prompt: Are user preferences and assistive technology compatibility considered?
questions.why: Contrast, forced colors, reduced motion and zoom may require hands-on assessment.

questions.prompt: Are languages and translated or localized experiences documented?
questions.why: Identify supported locales and any translation workflow.

questions.prompt: Does text handling account for Unicode and varied writing systems?
questions.why: Encoding and directionality should not be assumed from language alone.

questions.prompt: Are locale-sensitive formats and user input considered?
questions.why: Dates, numbers, addresses and sorting differ across locales.

questions.prompt: What personal or sensitive data does the project collect, process or transmit?
questions.why: Locate data flow descriptions and distinguish code behavior from policy claims.

questions.prompt: Are purpose limitation, data minimization and retention addressed?
questions.why: Policies may be incomplete and implementation may differ.

questions.prompt: Could the system enable tracking, profiling or unexpected data disclosure?
questions.why: Look for analytics, identifiers, telemetry and third-party integrations.

questions.prompt: Are trust boundaries, threats and security expectations documented?
questions.why: Consider threat models, known vulnerabilities and accepted risks.

questions.prompt: Are authentication, authorization, and permissions appropriate for the use case?
questions.why: Presence of an authentication package is not proof of its correctness.

questions.prompt: Are dependency, supply-chain and data integrity risks considered?
questions.why: Inspect available automation, release controls and advisories.

questions.prompt: Is the purpose, scope and architecture understandable to maintainers and adopters?
questions.why: Look for design documentation, specifications, ADRs or public APIs.

questions.prompt: Are compatibility, interoperability and graceful degradation considered?
questions.why: A declared feature may not work across all intended environments.

questions.prompt: Are versions, deprecations and public interfaces managed transparently?
questions.why: Review release notes and upgrade or migration information.

questions.prompt: Does the project discuss energy, computation, data-transfer or storage impacts?
questions.why: No energy or emissions estimate should be inferred from a repository keyword.

questions.prompt: Does it consider the lifetime of user devices, dependencies and supported environments?
questions.why: Compatibility, repairability and lifecycle can affect e-waste.

questions.prompt: Are environmental assumptions, trade-offs and measurement methods documented?
questions.why: Quantitative claims require methods, boundaries and reproducible measurements.

questions.prompt: Are transparency, open governance and social impacts considered?
questions.why: Look for governance, contribution and impacted-community participation.
